LESSON: POETRY 1.2.1 INTRODUCTION TO POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: INTRODUCTION TO ORAL LITERATURE Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sug
Topic 1.2: Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction to Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction to Poetry, part of INTRODUCTION TO ORAL LITERATURE Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sug in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we study poetry?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction to Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner speaks clearly and effectively while presenting the

elements of poems on a mind map and displays in class.

● Digital literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with technology when searching for the meaning and elements

of poetry from online sources.

Values:
● Unity: This is developed as the learner works with others when collecting varied poems from Kenya and organise in a

class portfolio.

● Respect: This is promoted as the learner listens to other’s views during group discussions on elements of poetry.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio economic issues: This is developed while the learner discusses the elements of a poem from Kenya on road

safety or environmental conservation.
